To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the variable-signal plus ongoing activity model provides a powerful framework for analyzing neurobiological time-series data, that a Bayesian differential component analysis approach can be used for extracting the variable-signal component from single-trial time series, and that the resulting ongoing activity can be analyzed by an adaptive autoregressive modeling approach that yields power, coherence and Granger-causality spectra.

(a) the event-related potential (ERP) can be estimated on a single trial level by a differentially variable components analysis strategy that is based on a variable-signal-plus-noise model; (b) after subtracting the ERP, the residual ongoing local field potentials (LFP) can be modeled as piecewise stationary stochastic processes, and (c) the LFPs can be decomposed into their constituent components by an adaptive multichannel autoregressive modeling approach that yields power,

(1) the variable signal plus ongoing activity model provides an accurate description of the neurobiological time course of evoked activity and ongoing activity, and (2) a Bayesian approach for the estimation of the event-related signal is more accurate than the traditional method based on averaging across trials.
